items.title: Tony Parenti and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-06-29
items.q: That's Popolini. Yeah. Yeah. You know, he's, uh, really fabulous when you come to think of it. Sure. Because he goes way back further than we do.

ctx.x: Well, the right guys do, of course, but he, uh, he told me he hadn't played drums since World War I.

Who's that? Jack Lane. He can still play. Well, the old man is still living. That's Popolini. Yeah. Yeah. You know, he's, uh, really fabulous when you come to think of it. Sure. Because he goes way back further than we do. And in his heyday, he was a big man because that was considered great to be able to book parades and, and get. And he put up a good band. Jack put up a good band. And he'd get all the best boys available, sure. But, uh, what was the name of that one jazz man that played the odd instrument that…
